subject: Network egress authorization & I/O capacity - private deploy scrub
messages:
From: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@metalworks.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: MetalWorks IT <ops@metalworks.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment — connectivity & disk throughput questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for last week's demo. Our security and infra teams are working through two items that will determine whether we can proceed with the on-prem pilot: egress authorization for model updates/telemetry, and guaranteed I/O capacity for model checkpoints and KV cache. I attached a rough network service diagram (metalworks-network-svc-diagram.pdf).

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood initiate outbound TLS connections only to a short allowlist (IP ranges / FQDNs)? How does the control-plane handshake look and which ports are required?
- For local NVMe-backed nodepools, what's the recommended IOPS and bandwidth envelope per replica for a 1.5B parameter model with 2k context?

We'd like to run a short I/O benchmark and validate egress rules before signing the PO. Can your team join a technical scrub tomorrow?

Paul
Head of Platform Engineering
MetalWorks Industries

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@metalworks.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity & disk throughput questions

Paul,

Appreciate the diagram — that's helpful. We can absolutely support a locked-down outbound pattern and a preflight I/O run. High-level answers below; we'll align with Dev and Ops on numbers in the scrub.

Outbound/connectivity
- Control plane: TLS outbound to a short FQDN allowlist (control.redwood-inference.com) over 443. Optionally we can provide a set of stable IP prefixes if your network team requires IP-based firewall rules; we update the prefix set on a scheduled cadence and publish a signed manifest.
- Telemetry/metrics: batched, periodic POSTs to telemetry endpoints; can be disabled for air-gapped installs.
- Model artifacts: we support both pushed (by CI/CD) and pull (agent outbound) modes. For pull mode the agent reaches out to artifacts.redwood-inference.com:443.

I/O guidance (initial)
- For 1.5B model at 2k context: recommend 1.5-2 GiB/s sustained bandwidth per active replica and 50k-100k read IOPS for KV-heavy workloads. Checkpoint writes are bursty; plan for 2x peak write bandwidth during model updates.

We'll run a micro-benchmark with your NVMe nodes; Dev will attach the script and expected CSV format. Proposed scrub: 2027-05-04 10:00 PT. Are you available?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Field Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@metalworks.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity & disk throughput questions

Paul / team,

Attaching the micro-benchmark we run for storage (io-benchmark-results.csv expected output). The script runs a mixed read/write profile that simulates KV cache hot-path and checkpoint write bursts. Attachment: redwood-storage-bench.zip (stub).

Quick notes:
- Run the script on the node you plan to dedicate to model replicas (not on a hypervisor / shared host).
- For NVMe in RAID-0 configurations we recommend leaving one spare device for rebuilds.
- We'll instrument and collect perf counters (blk_mq, nvme latency histograms) during the run.

If the benchmark shows sub-1 GiB/s sustained throughput or tail latency > 5ms at 95th percentile under our profile, we'll discuss a sizing change or throttled checkpoint cadence.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-storage-bench.zip (script + run instructions)
From: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@metalworks.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: MetalWorks IT <ops@metalworks.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity & disk throughput questions

Thanks — we ran the bench on two NVMe boxes in our staging rack this morning. Results summary attached (io-benchmark-results.csv). Key observations:
- Sustained read bandwidth ~0.9 GiB/s per node; 95th percentile read latency ~6.8ms under mixed load.
- Checkpoint writes peaked at ~3.8 GiB/s for a short burst (30s) on a single replica, causing transient GC on other services.

Notes / asks:
- Can Redwood enable checkpoint throttling and staggered rollouts to avoid simultaneous full-out writes?
- If we rely on agent-pull for model artifacts, what timeouts/retries should we provision on our proxy?

I'll schedule a short call to walk through the CSV with your team at 2027-05-04 13:30 PT.

-Paul

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@metalworks.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-05T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — connectivity & disk throughput questions

Paul — great session earlier. Recap and action items below (TL;DR first).

TL;DR: We can support your locked-down outbound model with an FQDN allowlist (optionally provide IP prefixes). We will enable checkpoint rate-limiting in the agent and recommend the following nodepool profile for pilot: 3x high-IO NVMe replicas (2.5 GiB/s expected each) + 1x staging replica for updates. We'll provide a hardened proxy timeout recipe and a signed IP manifest for your firewall team.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Redwood: Deliver signed IP prefix manifest + allowlist guidance (neha_kapoor) — ETA 2027-05-06 12:00 PT.
- Redwood Dev: Provide patched agent with checkpoint throttling + runbook for staggered rollouts (dev_patel) — ETA 2027-05-09.
- MetalWorks: Provision 3 NVMe replicas and re-run the provided benchmark after adding a spare device and disabling background GC (paul.henderson@metalworks.com) — ETA 2027-05-07.
- Both: Doc link with final checklist and run commands (shared Drive) — https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-metalworks-onprem-preflight

Follow-ups: Priyom and Laura will coordinate on the private-console onboarding and policy mapping once the network allowlist and I/O profile are confirmed. If all looks good we can convert the pilot into a reserved capacity contract.

Thanks everyone — I'll drop the signed manifest this afternoon and upload the redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx to the Drive.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Field Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment(s) referenced: metalworks-network-svc-diagram.pdf, io-benchmark-results.csv, redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx
